The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Formed in New York (1977)
podcast.body: The Plasmatics, a punk rock/metal band, were formed in New York in 1977 and led by singer Wendy O'Williams. "the Plasmatics, a punk rock slash metal band from New York, led by singer Wendy O'Williams that was formed in 1977."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Death by Suicide (1998)
podcast.body: Wendy O'Williams tragically died by suicide in 1998, walking into the woods near her Connecticut home, placing a bag over her head, and using a pistol. "She finally managed to kill herself in 1998. She walked into the woods near her home in Connecticut, put a bag over her head, and used a pistol."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: CBGB Roots
podcast.body: The Plasmatics began their career at CBGB, a venue famous for launching other punk and new wave bands like The Ramones, Talking Heads, and Blondie. "They started out at CBGB, the same place that gave us the remones and the talking hands of Blonday."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Destructive Stage Antics
podcast.body: The band was known for their willingness to do anything for a reaction, including using chainsaws to cut up items, smashing TV sets with sledgehammers, and blowing up objects like cars on stage. "using a chainsaw to cut up stuff on stage, taking a sledgehammer to TV sets, and they liked to blow stuff up. Whenever they could, that would include a car as part of their gig."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Discovered by Rod Swenson
podcast.body: Her transition into music was catalyzed by meeting Rod Swenson, a master of fine arts graduate, who convinced her to pursue a musical career, leading to the formation of The Plasmatics. "It was when she met a master of fine arts graduate named Rod Swenson, that she was persuaded to get into music."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Huge Popularity from Antics
podcast.body: Despite or because of their shocking antics, The Plasmatics became extremely popular, often playing two shows a night for multiple consecutive nights with long lines of fans awaiting entry. "But because of their antics, they ended up being huge. They could play two shows a night, multiple nights in a row, and still have lines down the block."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Obscenity Charge for Shaving Cream Outfit
podcast.body: Wendy O'Williams was once charged with obscenity for performing at a gig wearing nothing but shaving cream. "She was once charged with obscenity for appearing at a gig wearing nothing but shaving cream."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Post-Music Retirement and Suicide Attempts
podcast.body: After The Plasmatics broke up, Wendy O'Williams pursued acting and recorded some soul material before retiring. She subsequently made a series of suicide attempts, including one where she tried to stab herself in the heart but the knife got stuck in her sternum. "Then came a series of suicide attempts. Including the time she tried to jam a knife right into her own heart, but it became stuck in her sternum."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Wendy O'Williams' Radical Background
podcast.body: Wendy O'Williams, described as the most radical female singer of her era, originated from Colorado and had a past performing in live sex shows in Times Square and later in porn films before her music career. "She was originally from Colorado, but ended up in New York performing live sex shows and Times Square and later graduated to performing in porn films."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: `SCTV` Topless Compromise
podcast.body: When booked on the Canadian TV show `SCTV`, Wendy O'Williams refused to wear a top. A compromise was reached where a makeup artist painted her breasts black to conceal them on air. "When the Plasmatics were booked on the old Canadian TV show, SCTV, she refused to wear a top. The salvage, everything the compromise was to have the makeup artist paint her breasts black so you couldn't tell."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
